title: A Skid Steer and Its Centre of Rotation: Why Four Fixed Wheels Turn Only by Scrubbing, What That Costs, and Whether the Motors Can Pay

questions.question: How does a skid steer vehicle turn?
options: By steering one axle, as a car does
By driving the sides at different speeds and dragging the wheels sideways
By braking the inner wheels only
By tilting its wheels into the turn
questions.explanation: All four wheels point straight along the chassis. Turning means one side goes faster than the other and every wheel is dragged partly sideways.

questions.question: A chassis of 0.30 m by 0.25 m slides its front wheels in a pivot at:
questions.explanation: The angle of the slide at the front wheels is the arctangent of the wheelbase over the track: atan of 0.30 over 0.25. A square chassis would be 45 degrees.

questions.question: At chi 1.5 against 1.0, the centre of rotation for the same wheels was:
questions.explanation: The vehicle turns 1.5 times less for the same wheel speeds, so the point it turns about is 1.5 times further: 0.938 m against 0.625 m.

questions.question: Could two gear motors a side pivot a 10 kg vehicle on gravel?
options: No: it needed 34.5 N a side against 28.0 N
Yes: it needed 7.7 N a side
No: it needed 81.8 N a side
questions.explanation: Scrubbing four wheels sideways on gravel takes 34.5 N from each side, and two gear motors a side give 28.0 N. On ice it took 7.7 N.

questions.question: Why are skid steer machines built short?
options: A short, wide chassis slides its wheels at a smaller angle and needs less force to turn
Short machines have a lower centre of mass
To fit more wheels on each side
questions.explanation: The slide angle is atan of length over width, and the scrubbing force grows with the diagonal over the track. Long and narrow scrubs hardest.

questions.question: What does the ICR coefficient do to a differential drive model?
options: Makes the turn smaller by one over the coefficient, as if the track were wider
questions.explanation: A skid steer of coefficient 1.4 and a differential drive with an efficiency of one over 1.4 followed the same path to rounding.
